results.cause: The pod runs image "busybox:1.36" with command ["/app/payment-gateway","--listen=:8443"], but stock busybox contains no /app/payment-gateway binary. runc fails with "exec: \"/app/payment-gateway\": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory" (StartError, exit code 128). The rule finding mentions exit 127, but the actual exit code is 128 because the process never started. Its conclusion still holds: the command is missing from the image. Most likely the wrong image was set (busybox instead of the payment-gateway application image).
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image in deployment/payment-gateway to the actual payment-gateway application image that contains /app/payment-gateway, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<your-payment-gateway-image:tag>
If the image is already correct in your registry but the binary lives elsewhere, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].command to the real binary path inside that image
Verify locally that the image contains the binary: docker run --rm --entrypoint ls <image> -l /app/payment-gateway

results.cause: The migrate script exits 1 after reporting 'ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists' while running 'applying migration 0042_add_orders_index'. The migration is not idempotent: the index already exists, so every retry fails the same way. In this spec, the args also hard-code 'exit 1', so the container will fail regardless of database state until the script is changed.
fix: Make migration 0042_add_orders_index idempotent, e.g. use 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ...', or mark the migration as already applied in the migration tracking table if the index was created manually or by a partial earlier run.

Edit the init container 'migrate' args in deployment/orders-api: remove the unconditional 'exit 1', and only exit non-zero on a real failure. Then roll out with 'kubectl -n pfa-lab apply -f <manifest>' or 'kubectl -n pfa-lab edit deployment orders-api'.
If the index is a leftover from a failed run and should be recreated, drop 'orders_idx' in the database and let the init container re-run the migration.

results.cause: The startup script checks `if [ -z "$DATABASE_URL" ]` and exits 1, logging "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set". The container env only defines DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL; DATABASE_URL is not set. Separately, the script echoes the DB password to the logs (shown as <REDACTED:password>), which leaks a credential.
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to the api container's env in deployment/checkout-api. If it contains credentials, source it from a Secret: `env: - name: DATABASE_URL, valueFrom: secretKeyRef: {name: <secret>, key: <key>}`.
Apply the change and confirm the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api`.
Remove `password=$DB_PASSWORD` from the startup echo so the password is no longer written to the logs. Rotate that password, since it has already been logged.

results.cause: The tag is misspelled: "1.36.1-uclbic" looks like a typo of the busybox uClibc variant tag "1.36.1-uclibc" (missing the 'i'). The registry answers "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found" (rpc error code = NotFound), so this is a wrong tag, not an auth or network problem.
fix: Correct the image in the Deployment, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` (or set spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image to busybox:1.36.1-uclibc in the manifest and re-apply).
If unsure the tag exists, verify first with `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` or `crane ls busybox`, or use a plain tag like busybox:1.36.1.
Watch the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront`. The rollout is already marked ProgressDeadlineExceeded, and the new image change starts a fresh rollout.

results.cause: The image field has two tags: "busybox:1.36:latest". An image reference can have only one ":tag", so the kubelet fails with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). This often happens when a template appends ":latest" to a value that already contains a tag.
fix: Change spec.template.spec.containers[name=worker].image in deployment/notify-worker to a single tag, e.g. "busybox:1.36": kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36
If the image is built from a template or variables (Helm values, kustomize images, CI), make sure the tag is not appended twice, i.e. image repo "busybox" plus tag "1.36".
Optionally pin a specific version tag rather than "latest" to keep rollouts reproducible.

results.cause: Pulls are routed through the mirror http://registry-mirror:1273, which answered the manifest HEAD request with "500 Internal Server Error" for registry registry.pfa-lab.invalid. A 500 from the mirror means it failed to fetch from the upstream. It is not a 'not found' or 'unauthorized' answer. The upstream hostname "registry.pfa-lab.invalid" uses the reserved .invalid TLD, which never resolves, so the mirror most likely cannot reach that registry. If the hostname is intentional, the mirror itself is failing.
fix: Correct the registry hostname in the image reference: set spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image in deployment/billing-ui to the real registry, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<correct-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0

If registry.pfa-lab.invalid is the intended registry, fix the mirror at registry-mirror:1273 so it can resolve and reach that upstream: check its logs and upstream/proxy configuration, then let the pod retry or delete it to re-pull.
Alternatively, bypass the mirror by pushing billing/ui:3.2.0 to a registry the node can reach, or load it directly onto node desktop-control-plane, then point the image field at it.

results.cause: The container command allocates more memory than the limit allows: it runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0`, i.e. a 300M allocation, while resources.limits.memory is 200Mi. The last log line before the kill is "stress: info: [1] dispatching hogs: 0 cpu, 0 io, 1 vm, 0 hdd", right after "cache warmup: loading remaining 100MB". The workload's intended footprint (~300MB) is larger than the 200Mi limit, so this is an undersized limit, not a leak.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) on container cache in statefulset/session-cache above the ~300M peak plus headroom, e.g. limits.memory: 384Mi (or 448Mi as the rule suggests): kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"384Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"384Mi"}]'
Alternatively, if 200Mi is the intended budget, reduce the allocation in args, e.g. change --vm-bytes 300M to a value well below 200Mi (such as 150M).
After the change, confirm the pod becomes Ready and check usage with: kubectl -n pfa-lab top pod session-cache-0

results.cause: The container command allocates 250MB on purpose ("exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0", log: "loading 250MB of order history into memory"), but resources.limits.memory is "128Mi". It is OOMKilled (exit code 137) within the same second it starts (started_at and finished_at both 2026-11-02T15:22:34). This is a fixed oversize allocation, not a gradual leak.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory on container worker above the 250MB working set plus overhead, e.g. 384Mi (256Mi is too tight for 250M plus process overhead). Also raise requests.memory to about 300Mi so the scheduler reserves enough: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=384Mi --requests=memory=300Mi
Or reduce what the worker loads at once so it fits under 128Mi, e.g. lower --vm-bytes, or in the real app, load order history in smaller batches.
After the change, confirm the new pod stays Running with kubectl -n pfa-lab get pods -w and check usage with kubectl top pod.

results.cause: The container is configured to hold far more memory than its limit allows: its args run "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0" and it logs "log-shipper starting, buffering 200MB of logs in memory", but resources.limits.memory is "64Mi". It hits the limit within a second of starting (started_at and finished_at both 2026-11-02T15:27:26) and terminates with OOMKilled, exit code 137. It has restarted 3 times. 128Mi would still be too low for a 200M buffer.
fix: Reduce what the container allocates to fit the limit, for example change --vm-bytes 200M to roughly 48M (the log-shipper's in-memory buffer size) so it stays under 64Mi.

Or, if 200MB of buffering is really needed, raise the log-shipper container's resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) to at least 256Mi to leave headroom above the 200M allocation. Example: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi
After the change, confirm the pod becomes Ready and restarts stop: kubectl -n pfa-lab get pod -l app=<label> -w (or check deployment/search-api availability).

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores). That is almost certainly a unit mistake for "4000m" (4 cores). The scheduler rejects the pod with "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu", and preemption cannot help.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu from "4000"/"4k" to "4000m", or lower it to what the app actually needs (e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m).
Make sure the new request fits the node's allocatable CPU (kubectl describe node). If 4 cores do not fit on the single node, lower the request further or add a larger node.
After the rollout, confirm the new pod schedules and the deployment leaves ProgressDeadlineExceeded (kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ml-trainer).

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab. The kubelet reports FailedMount x7: "MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume \"templates\" : configmap \"email-templates\" not found". The container cannot start until the volume mounts.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the right namespace, for example: kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>. If it is defined in a manifest, apply it with kubectl -n pfa-lab apply -f <file>.

If the configmap exists under a different name or namespace, set spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.name in deployment/email-sender to the correct name, and keep it in namespace pfa-lab.
If the templates are optional, set spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.optional: true so the pod can start without them.
The kubelet retries the mount automatically once the configmap exists. If the pod stays stuck, run: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/email-sender

results.cause: The pod spec has nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, and the scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". No node carries the label hardware=gpu-a100, and preemption cannot help.
fix: If the workload does not need a GPU node (the container is busybox:1.36 running `sleep 3600`), remove spec.template.spec.nodeSelector.hardware from deployment/video-encoder: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector/hardware"}]'
If it should run on a specific node, label that node: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
Otherwise change the nodeSelector to a label that actually exists on a node (compare against kubectl get nodes --show-labels), or add an A100 node pool carrying hardware=gpu-a100.

results.cause: The readiness probe requests "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves /healthz. The container command writes only /www/healthz and the log says "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz". The port (http=80) is correct, so httpd answers, but it returns 404 for /ready ("Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404", x17).
fix: Change the readiness probe path in the deployment spec from /ready to /healthz: spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path: /healthz (e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]').
Alternatively, if /ready is the intended endpoint, make the app serve it, for example by adding 'echo ok > /www/ready' to the container args.
Verify with: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/catalog-api

results.cause: The app spends about 45 seconds replaying its journal before it starts httpd on port 80 (log: "ledger-api replaying journal, this takes about 45 seconds"; script runs "sleep 45" before "exec httpd -f -p 80"). The liveness probe (HTTP /healthz port=http, initialDelaySeconds=2, periodSeconds=3, failureThreshold=2) gives it only about 8 seconds, so it gets "connect: connection refused" and the kubelet kills the container (exit code 137). The probe port and path are correct; the startup budget is just too short. The 'listening on :80' line never appears in either log.
fix: Add a startupProbe to container api with the same check (httpGet path /healthz, port http), periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 15 (~75 s budget). Liveness only starts after it succeeds.
Alternatively raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to at least 60 (e.g. 60-75), though a startupProbe is preferred.
Optionally relax livenessProbe to periodSeconds: 10 and failureThreshold: 3 to avoid restarts on brief hiccups.
Add a readinessProbe on /healthz so the pod is not marked Ready before httpd is listening (it currently shows Ready=True with no readiness probe).

results.cause: The liveness probe is "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80 -h /www", logs "inventory-api listening on :80" and declares only port http=80/TCP. Every probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused". After failure_threshold 2, the kubelet kills the container with exit code 137 even though httpd was serving /healthz on port 80.
fix: In the StatefulSet inventory-api, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port from 8080 to 80 (or to the named port "http").

Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'. If the pod is not replaced, delete inventory-api-0 so it is recreated with the new spec.
Optional: add a readinessProbe on the same port and path, and consider a slightly longer initialDelaySeconds and timeoutSeconds than 3s and 1s.
